_meta.purpose: The new constitution, as a four-step track. The 8 February 2026 referendum approved drafting one (60.16% yes, 69.65% turnout). Chapters 1 and 2 are not on the table. Bhumjaithai tables nothing radical: the furthest most parts go is a moderate reformist tilt. Two go one step further (every governor elected, the Constitutional Court reconstituted), and the Senate makes both hard to pass.
_meta.stances: Party and Senate stance on each position, -2 (opposes) to +2 (supports). Positions are ordered from least to most reformist; `score` is the reform score.
_meta.vote: Each changed clause goes to a joint sitting: yes >= 351 of 700 and at least 67 of 200 senators. A clause that fails reverts to the current text.
_meta.singapore: Singapore-lite positions (sgLite) score -1. They strengthen the state rather than open it. They pay in full only with civil service reform and anti-corruption enforcement done (competentIf); otherwise execution gains are halved and approval falls. Any position can carry competentIf: electing every governor pays in full only with the Electoral Integrity Act enforced, and without it sets withoutSets (the bosses capture the governorships) and shows its warning.

positions.label: Keep
positions.text: The 2024 self-selection system and every current power.

positions.label: Adjust
positions.text: Selection kept, but the candidate groups are opened up and block voting is banned.

positions.label: Tilt
positions.text: Selection kept. The Senate loses its one-third veto over constitutional amendments.

positions.label: Multi-member
positions.text: Larger constituencies electing slates of three, winner takes all, as in Singapore's group constituencies. Thailand used block voting before 1997 and in 2007. Applies at the next general election.
400 constituency seats and 100 party-list seats, two ballots.
Ten constituencies become list seats. Applies at the next general election.
Twenty-five constituencies become list seats. Still parallel, not MMP. Applies at the next general election.

positions.label: Keep
positions.text: The Court and its power to dissolve parties, unchanged.

positions.label: Adjust
positions.text: The panel that selects judges is widened, with one member nominated by the opposition.

positions.label: Tilt
positions.text: Dissolving a party needs a two-thirds vote of the Court.

positions.label: Reconstitute
positions.text: The Court is rebuilt: judges confirmed by two-thirds of the House to staggered nine-year terms, and dissolving a party limited to proven electoral fraud, brought by the Election Commission.

positions.label: Delivery unit
positions.text: Governors stay appointed and report to a Prime Minister's delivery unit with binding targets, on the Singapore civil service and Malaysian PEMANDU model.

positions.label: Keep
positions.text: Governors appointed by the Interior Ministry.

positions.label: Adjust
positions.text: Elected-governor pilot in Chiang Mai, Phuket and Khon Kaen.

positions.label: Tilt
positions.text: Pilot in ten provinces, from Chonburi and Rayong to Songkhla and Ubon Ratchathani, and a modestly larger local share of revenue.

positions.label: Elect them all
positions.text: Every province elects its governor from 2031, as Bangkok does, and keeps a third of the revenue raised in it. The Interior Ministry's provincial line is wound down.
positions.warning: No Electoral Integrity Act enforced. The governorships go to whoever pays the canvassers: the provincial bosses take them, the reform loses most of its effect, and the machine parties gain at the 2030 count.

positions.label: Paternalist
positions.text: The Singapore model. Duties sit beside rights: public order, social harmony, responsible expression. The state gains wider powers over assembly and online content.

positions.label: Keep
positions.text: The current rights chapter.

positions.label: Adjust
positions.text: Community rights over land and the environment.

positions.label: Tilt
positions.text: Community rights, and a constitutional right to government information.

positions.label: Integrity bureau
positions.text: The investigators of the anti-corruption commission and the Election Commission merged into one bureau that reports to the Prime Minister, on Singapore's CPIB model. The cabinet appoints its director.

positions.label: Keep
positions.text: Selection committees choose the Election Commission, the anti-corruption commission, the Ombudsman and the State Audit Office. The Senate confirms them.

positions.label: Adjust
positions.text: Open nominations, public hearings, and two opposition seats on every selection committee. The Senate still confirms.
